title: Introduce routing rule compiler and async fallback coordinator; prune regional shards
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: The current smart-routing hotpath performs synchronous policy evaluation and fallback selection with coarse-grained locks and on-path region shard lookups. This results in increased p95 latency during traffic bursts, elevated CPU on control-plane goroutines, and slow startup times when many region shards are materialized.

Goal: Replace the on-request synchronous evaluator with a routing rule compiler that precomputes a compact, immutable decision graph per policy version, and introduce an Async Fallback Coordinator (AFC) that performs capacity-checks and fallback selection off the request critical path. Additionally, prune and lazily materialize region shards to reduce memory and startup overhead. The end state should reduce routing p95 under burst loads by ~30-50% and remove a class of locking-related production incidents.

Scope:
- Implement a routing rule compiler that consumes policy definitions and emits an immutable, versioned decision graph serialized for fast in-memory lookup.
- Add AFC service that subscribes to compiled policy versions and maintains ephemeral capacity hints; AFC responds to routing layer with fallback targets asynchronously.
- Change request hotpath to consult compiled decision graph and submit a non-blocking fallback query to AFC (with a short timeout), falling back to precomputed conservative defaults if AFC times out.
- Prune region shard lifecycle: lazy materialization, eviction of cold shards, and faster warm-path creation.
- Remove on-path global locks in router hotpath; replace with atomic pointers to immutable structures to allow lock-free reads.
- Upgrade async runtime and relevant crates (tokio 1.x bump, smallvec / dashmap upgrades) where needed and audit for await points in hotpath.
- Add integration tests and chaos tests for AFC timeouts, race conditions with KV cache, and multi-region failovers.

Out of scope: full replacement of legacy policy DSL (we will compile current DSL), large refactors of KV cache internals (only surface fixes to avoid races), and UI changes in Console (separate PM story).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Router uses compiled decision graph in prod canary with feature flag enabled.
2) AFC responds to 95% of fallback queries within 15ms under normal load; on AFC timeout, router falls back to precomputed conservative target.
3) p95 routing latency under synthetic burst (300 qps, 50ms model latencies) is <= 260ms (baseline 420ms).
4) No increase in error-rate or incorrect regional affinity decisions during canary.
5) Automated integration tests for fallback races present and passing in CI.
implementation_notes:
- Compiler: Rust binary in router/service that watches policy store and emits versioned blobs (protobuf). Keep serialized format backwards-compatible.
- AFC: lightweight async service deployed as sidecar/centralized tier; exposes gRPC with short deadlines. Accepts multiplexed queries.
- Hotpath changes: load decision graph via atomic pointer swap on update; remove locks for read path.
- Shard pruning: add LRU eviction for region shards with metrics and debugging tags.
- Feature flags: routing_new_compiler (global), routing_afc_enabled (per-customer).
- Telemetry: new tracing span 'routing.compiler.apply' and metrics: routing.compiled_version, routing.afc_latency_ms.p50/p95/p99, routing.shard_evictions.
risks_and_mitigation:
- AFC becomes central dependency: mitigate with timeouts and conservative in-router defaults; implement circuit-breaker and degrade to static fallback targets.
- KV cache race with fallback rewrite: isolate by adding single-writer invariants and add a short compatibility shim for reads during migration.
- Serialization compatibility: keep two-format readers for 3 weeks rollout, monitor errors.
- Rollback: feature flags + traffic-splitting with automatic rollback if p95 regresses >15%.
rollout_plan:
1) Deploy compiler and AFC to staging; run integration load tests.
2) Canary deployment: enable feature flag in us-east-1 for 5% traffic for 48h. Monitor p95, errors, routing decision correctness.
3) Expand to us-west-2 and eu-west-1 at 25% for 48h.
4) Global enable at 100% with one-week monitoring window.
5) Post-rollout: run backfill job to remove old compiled blobs after 30 days.
Feature flags: routing_new_compiler, routing_afc_enabled. KPI gating: routing.p95, routing.error_rate, afc.success_rate.
